target_customer: Consumers with large personal media libraries, paying 20 dollars per month for unlimited storage or using a free 20GB plan
problem: Media files filled local disks and syncing them to cloud drives still consumed space; Streem stored one copy in the cloud and streamed files on demand.
business_model: Consumer subscription: 20 dollars per month unlimited storage, free tier of 20GB (April 2014 launch coverage)
product_category: Cloud storage and media streaming file system

founders.name: Ritik Malhotra
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

founders.name: Tanooj Luthra
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a career path including Box, Coinbase, Brex and OpenAI after Streem; none are documented as prior to founding.

founders.name: Samvit Ramadurgam
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: A cloud backed virtual file system with on the fly media conversion and streaming (StreemFS) on Windows and Mac needed filesystem driver and streaming engineering from a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: The filesystem streaming approach was distinctive, but storage giants cut prices and could add streaming; Box bought it for the technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Box acquired it on June 16 2014 for undisclosed cash and stock, about two months after launch, to fill a desktop access gap.

market_need_then: Falling storage prices and faster internet made cloud storage competitive; Box and others lacked a desktop streaming file experience per TechCrunch reporting; no usage figures were found.

branding.domain_note: streem.com now redirects to frontdoorhome.com because a later unrelated company named Streem was bought by Frontdoor in 2019.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer pitch about a magical drive in the cloud with unlimited space

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found. Coverage of the acquisition included a Computerworld piece calling it the real world Pied Piper, which is press attention to the technology, not the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Launched in April 2014 and sold two months later; no brand evidence beyond a misspelled word name, and a later Streem company created confusion.

outcome_analysis: Streem built StreemFS, a cloud file system that streams media on demand, launched it in April 2014 with 20 dollar unlimited storage after raising 875 thousand dollars, and was bought by Box two months later. The team of four joined Box and the consumer product was wound down with users moved to a 50GB Box tier. Terms were undisclosed, so this reads as a technology acquisition rather than a proven market win.
notes: Competition is as of the April 2014 launch; no source dated to the 2012 batch was found. Seed total of 875K is per TechCrunch headline snippet from search; amount only from that source plus an aggregator listing about 880K, treated as one round. A 2017 Portland Streem (AR video) and its Frontdoor acquisition in 2019 is a different company; its funding is excluded. streem.com redirects to frontdoorhome.com. Tanooj Luthra's YC career string tags Streem as W19, a conflict with the S12 batch, and likely refers to the later company. Competitor list is empty because only April 2014 launch coverage was found, naming Dropbox and Google Drive; nothing dated near the 2012 batch.
